meta.falsification: A finite affine spectrum that is not the set of divisors of its maximum, or a spectrum that is not divisor-closed, would contradict the (proved) Theorem 1 of proofs/paper/C13.md and reveal an implementation error.
meta.hypothesis: H-C13-3: affine spectra are exactly the sets {N : a fixed polynomial system has a root mod N}; they are divisor-closed and closed under coprime products, every finite one is the set of divisors of a single integer, and the infinite ones are governed by the Q-gcd of the system (a classical quadratic/cubic residue condition plus finitely many exceptional primes).
meta.methodology: Evaluate both sides as linear forms with coefficients in Z[a]; the law's affine system is the set of coefficient differences. Group laws by system, then systems by spectrum. For each system compute the gcd over Q[a]; if it is constant, bound the spectrum by the gcd of the pairwise resultants R and find the largest prime powers dividing R that admit a common root; otherwise record the gcd polynomial. Look up every infinite spectrum in the OEIS and record the hits.
meta.question: For every law s = t over {x,y,z} with at most 4 leaves per side (up to renaming and exchange of sides), and every law over {x,y} with at most 5 leaves per side, which sets of N admit an affine anchored model x*y = x + a*y + 1 (mod N)? Which arithmetic sets occur?
meta.title: Atlas of affine anchored spectra for all laws with at most 4 leaves per side (and 2-variable laws with at most 5)
